brooklyn:76.20.4.name: Unidentified maker
brooklyn:76.20.4.detail: The catalogue identifies this object as Luba and records its materials. It gives no individual maker's name.

brooklyn:76.20.4.name: Trained Luba interpreters
brooklyn:76.20.4.role: Role described for a separately catalogued example
brooklyn:76.20.4.detail: The public museum article describes a specialised role. It does not identify people who used the Brooklyn object.

hpmm:1105-0001.name: Shinichi Tetsutani
hpmm:1105-0001.detail: The Peace Database preserves his name alongside the tricycle. The object is connected to the Hiroshima bombing of 6 August 1945.

hpmm:1105-0001.name: Nobuo Tetsutani
hpmm:1105-0001.detail: The museum's receiving entry lists Nobuo as donor and gives 6 September 1985.

hpmm:1105-0001.name: Nobuo Tetsutani
hpmm:1105-0001.role: Father whose remembrance was publicly reported
hpmm:1105-0001.detail: In a separate account ICAN attributes to Nobuo a wish for a peaceful world where children can play.

loc:2021667561.name: Nasir al-Din Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn al-Hajj al-Amin al-Tawathi al-Ghalawi
loc:2021667561.detail: The exhibit identifies the author of the treatise that discusses using stellar motion to locate seasonal beginnings.

loc:2021667561.name: Unidentified copyist
loc:2021667561.detail: The exhibit dates the copy to 1733 and gives no name for the copyist.

loc:2021667561.name: Mamma Haidara Commemorative Library
loc:2021667561.detail: The Library of Congress catalogue names the Timbuktu library as the original's holder. Its exhibit credits the library's loan.

cma:1929.566.1.name: Unidentified carver
cma:1929.566.1.detail: The catalogue describes the wooden foot support and separate toe peg. It does not identify a named wearer.

cma:1996.268.name: Unidentified maker
cma:1996.268.detail: The catalogue lists wood and colorant and assigns a style without identifying a named maker.

cma:1929.356.name: Unidentified maker
cma:1929.356.detail: The catalogue records a date by 1928 and discusses hats made for travellers around Ekibondo. Its date and setting do not supply this maker’s name.

met:2007.447.name: Unidentified maker
met:2007.447.detail: The accession lists brass and fibre. The record supplies no name of a maker or wearer.

met:2005.408.2.name: Xhosa or Mfengu artist
met:2005.408.2.detail: The artist field leaves both attributions open. The record gives no individual name.

met:1995.64.15.name: Unidentified Kru artist
met:1995.64.15.detail: The author field assigns a Kru attribution. The accession describes a fired terracotta core beneath the brass.

nmafa:2002-10-3.name: Unidentified Luba maker
nmafa:2002-10-3.role: Catalogue attribution of this ingot group
nmafa:2002-10-3.detail: The catalogue lists five copper-alloy ingots. Its average measurements do not identify individual casting hands.

nmafa:89-4-2.name: Maria Theresa
nmafa:89-4-2.role: Historical figure represented on the coin
nmafa:89-4-2.detail: The coin shows Maria Theresa on one side. The named subject of the portrait and the people who made or used this particular coin are different roles.

met:1977.224.5a-d.name: Akan artist
met:1977.224.5a-d.detail: The catalogue gives a collective artist attribution and a probable geographical range. It does not identify the scale operator.

met:1977.224.6a-b.name: Unidentified maker
met:1977.224.6a-b.detail: The catalogue identifies a two-part gold-dust box without naming an individual maker or owner.

met:1999.47.69.name: Unidentified Middle Niger maker
met:1999.47.69.role: Qualified catalogue attribution of the vessel
met:1999.47.69.detail: The record assigns a qualified Middle Niger attribution and describes an impressed surface. It leaves the original contents open.

met:2018.356.name: Unobadula
met:2018.356.role: Name used by the catalogue’s stylistic attribution
met:2018.356.detail: The art history entry discusses a comparable group of sculptors. The listed attribution is distinct from a signed maker identification.

met:1972.63a-b.name: “Master of the Heraldic Ship”
met:1972.63a-b.role: Catalogue attribution used for an Edo-Bini carver
met:1972.63a-b.detail: The Met uses this art-historical name. It does not establish a personal name or confirm the possible patron.

met:1996.456.name: Chokwe artist
met:1996.456.detail: The artist field gives a Chokwe attribution. The geographical entry leaves Angola or the Democratic Republic of the Congo open.

met:89.4.926.name: Unidentified Ganda maker
met:89.4.926.detail: The catalogue identifies the construction of the instrument without naming a performer for this example.

cma:1929.343.name: Unidentified maker
cma:1929.343.detail: The museum documents a purchase in Kampala. Its purchase location identifies a point in custody rather than this maker’s home.

nmafa:84-14-7.name: Unidentified maker
nmafa:84-14-7.role: Maker of the Inland Niger Delta-style ring
nmafa:84-14-7.detail: The maker and exact use are open. The museum compares this ring with other forms that have different uses.

met:89.4.498.name: Unidentified Mandinka maker
met:89.4.498.detail: The record locates this example in Senegambia. It discusses remembered origins of the kora tradition separately from the identity of its maker.

met:89.4.473.name: Unidentified Fulbe maker
met:89.4.473.detail: The museum describes the trough and gives several possible places. It has no name for the person who made the example.

met:89.4.2035.name: Unidentified Igbo maker
met:89.4.2035.role: Maker of the catalogued ubo akwara
met:89.4.2035.detail: The record attributes the instrument to Igbo people and describes the individual flexible sticks without naming a maker or player.
